threads.body: The attribute-key naming is not unconditional: `CapturedMessageHeadersUtil` preserves dashes in v3 preview. This new public API documentation should describe both modes so callers do not query the wrong key.

replies.body:
Addressed in 46094a6b06460798b6ef888074d8a582a34ca13e.

Analysis: CapturedMessageHeadersUtil replaces dashes with underscores only when the v3 preview mode is disabled. The new selector Javadocs described only that default behavior, so callers using v3 preview could look up the wrong attribute key. Documenting the otel.instrumentation.common.v3-preview exception across every exposed builder aligns the API contract with the shared key-generation logic.

Upsides: Callers can derive the correct captured-header attribute key in both modes, and all sibling builder APIs now describe the behavior consistently.

Downsides: The API documentation is slightly longer; no runtime behavior changes.

threads.body: [General] This deprecated alias no longer preserves its exact-name behavior: `IncludeExclude` interprets `*` and `?` as globs, so a previously literal value such as `foo*` (or `*`) can suddenly capture many headers and expose sensitive values. The changelog promises that deprecated methods select the same headers; retain a literal-name path for this method instead of converting through the glob selector.

replies.body:
Addressed in 887ff341191c9e4bc97b91e2af78ceb10163b3d9.

Analysis: The code intentionally follows the gRPC and servlet selector migrations by treating deprecated collections as include-only selector aliases. Messaging never documented the MDC-specific legacy wildcard behavior that required a separate literal predicate in the logging migrations. The defect was the changelog sentence promising unchanged selection despite the intentional glob alias semantics, so I corrected that statement instead of adding a second matching mode to the shared public selector API.

Upsides: The documented migration now matches the implementation and related selector precedents, while the shared IncludeExclude API retains one consistent matching model.

Downsides: A deprecated value containing `*` or `?` gains glob semantics; this is now explicit, and these experimental properties and alpha APIs may be removed in the next minor release.

threads.body: [General] `SelectorConfig.resolve` converts the deprecated `capture_headers` list into an `IncludeExclude`, which changes legacy exact names containing `*` or `?` into glob patterns. That contradicts the compatibility promise and can unexpectedly capture sensitive headers; resolve deprecated messaging values through a literal-name path while keeping glob matching only for the new selector.

threads.body: [General] This deprecated alias now treats `*` and `?` in formerly exact header names as glob metacharacters. Existing callers can therefore capture additional, potentially sensitive headers despite the stated compatibility guarantee; preserve literal matching for `setCapturedHeaders` rather than translating it directly to `IncludeExclude`.
